adjudication_records.issue_text: error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder changed from {{0}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax ({0}, {2,choice,...}), which likely breaks substitution in React-based account UI and admin UI frontends, showing raw placeholders to users

adjudication.rationale: In the React app theme message bundles (`js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`), `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from i18n-style interpolation `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` to single-brace `MessageFormat`/`ChoiceFormat` syntax (`{0}`, `{2,choice,...}`). The diff does not show any corresponding change in the JS frontends’ formatting/interpolation logic, so this is a concrete, diff-grounded risk of runtime substitution breaking and users seeing raw `{0}` / `{2,choice,...}` text in the account/admin UIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lithuanian totpStep1 message replaced with Italian text, showing wrong-language instruction to Lithuanian users
verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException on I/O failures (including missing derived English file), breaking error propagation contract and masking all other findings in the verification run

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()`, `verifySafeHtml()` is called inside a `try { ... } catch (IOException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException(...) }`, but `verifySafeHtml()` itself catches `IOException` when loading both the target bundle and the derived English bundle and rethrows `new RuntimeException(...)` (see both `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(...) }` blocks). That means missing/unreadable properties (including the computed `englishFile`) will escape as an unchecked `RuntimeException`, bypassing the intended `MojoExecutionException` error propagation and aborting the verification early, potentially masking other collected `messages` findings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: containsHtml HTML_TAGS pattern only detects lowercase tags, so uppercase tags like <B> or <EM> cause POLICY_NO_HTML to be wrongly applied, producing false 'Illegal HTML' failures

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml(), HTML_TAGS is defined as `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which only matches lowercase tag names. Since the policy choice is `containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML`, any English message containing uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g., `<B>`, `<EM>`) would be misclassified as containing no HTML and thus validated with POLICY_NO_HTML, leading to false "Illegal HTML" failures for translations containing the same HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst which removes the first occurrence of the anchor string rather than the matched occurrence, potentially stripping the wrong anchor and producing false 'Didn't find anchor tag' errors for reordered anchors

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, `replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` does remove the first occurrence of the matching anchor substring, but within this loop it is only executed when `matcher.group()` equals `englishMatcher.group()`. Since the loop walks anchors left-to-right and removes one matching occurrence each time, this does not verifiably “strip the wrong anchor” in a way that would then cause the "Didn't find anchor tag" message. That message is added in the `else` branch (when the next English anchor doesn’t match), i.e., before any `replaceFirst` effect could produce it. Reordered anchors would be rejected due to the sequential `englishMatcher.find()` comparison (order sensitivity), not because `replaceFirst` removed the wrong occurrence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifyDuplicateKeysDetected test assertion weakened from contains() to hasItem(), masking any extra unexpected messages the verifier emits for the fixture

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.verifyDuplicateKeysDetected, the assertion changed from `Matchers.contains(...)` (which requires the list to match exactly, with no extra items) to `Matchers.hasItem(...)` (which only requires at least one matching item). This does weaken the test and could allow the verifier to emit additional unexpected messages for the duplicate-keys fixture without failing the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: normalizeValue email branch only strips the exact quoted RTL style attribute (style="direction: rtl;"), so variants with different quoting, spacing, or attribute order fail with a confusing 'Illegal HTML' message

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue`, the email-specific exception only removes the exact literal substring ` style="direction: rtl;"` via `value.replaceAll(Pattern.quote(" style=\"direction: rtl;\""), "")`. Any equivalent RTL markup with different spacing, single quotes, additional CSS, or different attribute formatting/order will not be stripped, and the OWASP sanitizer (which does not allow `style`) will modify it, causing `sanitized` != `value` and producing an `Illegal HTML` message. This is a real false-positive defect in the newly introduced HTML verification logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled RuntimeException when derived English sibling file path doesn't exist, aborting the verification run instead of recording a problem in messages

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the code derives an English sibling file path (englishFile = file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll(...)) and then unconditionally tries to load it via new FileInputStream(englishFile). If that derived file does not exist, a FileNotFoundException (IOException) is caught and rethrown as a new RuntimeException ("unable to read file ..."). This RuntimeException is not handled in verify() (which only catches IOException around Files.readString), so the entire verification run can abort rather than adding an entry to the messages list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English reference file path derived via fragile regex string munging with replaceAll, vulnerable to path-structure drift

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English reference path is derived via string regex munging on the absolute path: `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This approach is inherently coupled to the current repo directory naming and filename locale-suffix conventions; if those drift (or if the regex matches an unintended substring in the path), `englishFile` can be miscomputed and the code will fail by throwing `RuntimeException` when opening the derived file. The diff shows this new logic and the hard-coded assumptions, but it doesn’t prove it’s currently broken for existing paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: replaceAll treats its first argument as a regex, a latent trap if path patterns change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `replaceAll(...)` calls (e.g., `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")`), and `replaceAll` does interpret the first argument as a regex. However, in this specific usage the pattern is a fixed literal string without regex metacharacters that would change matching semantics, and the second `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` is intentionally regex-based. The finding’s claim of a “latent trap if path patterns change” is speculative and not a concrete, verifiable issue shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing English key falls back to empty string and applies POLICY_NO_HTML, causing false positives on legitimate HTML in translations

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that if an English key is missing, getEnglishValue() returns "" and verifySafeHtml() will then select POLICY_NO_HTML because containsHtml("") is false. However, the new logic explicitly enforces: “Only if the English source string contains HTML we also allow HTML in the translation”. Under that rule, a translation containing HTML when the English source is missing (or has no HTML) is intended to be flagged, not a “false positive”. The claim that such HTML would be “legitimate” is not supported or verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sanitizer allowlist only permits br/p/strong/b, so English strings with other benign tags like <em> get stripped, producing build-breaking false positives

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties, when the English source contains any HTML (containsHtml matches tags like <em>), the sanitizer policy used is POLICY_SOME_HTML, which only allows elements br/p/strong/b. Any other tags present in the English string (e.g., <em>) would be removed by policy.sanitize(value), and the code then compares sanitized vs. original value and reports "Illegal HTML" if they differ. The diff doesn’t show an actual existing English message using <em>, so the claim that this is currently build-breaking can’t be verified from the diff, but the allowlist limitation and potential for false positives is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor-comparison logic pairs Nth anchors positionally, misaligning on repeated or reordered identical anchors and reporting spurious 'Didn't find anchor tag' errors

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), anchors in the translated string are compared to anchors in the English string by advancing englishMatcher one step per translated anchor (englishMatcher.find()) and requiring exact equality of the current groups. This enforces positional/ordering equality rather than the stated intent (“Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key.”). If a translation reorders multiple distinct ... segments while keeping the same set of allowed anchors, the first mismatched position will trigger the “Didn't find anchor tag … in original string” message even though the tag exists later in the English string (spurious failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing via value.replaceFirst after matcher.find mutates the string being iterated, which can skip matches

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` is created once and then iterates over the *original* `value` content via `while (matcher.find())`. Reassigning `value = value.replaceFirst(...)` does not mutate the string being iterated by `matcher` (Java `String` is immutable, and the `Matcher` keeps operating on the original input). Therefore the specific claim that this “mutates the string being iterated, which can skip matches” is not verifiable from the diff and is essentially a misread of how `Matcher`/`String` work here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric unescaping (unescapeHtml4 before sanitizing vs. once after) can make equality check differ for benign strings, producing false 'Illegal HTML' verdicts

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `normalizeValue()` unescapes HTML entities on both the translated `value` and the `englishValue` *before* sanitization, and then `verifySafeHtml()` also unescapes the sanitizer output (`sanitized = unescapeHtml4(sanitized)`) before comparing. That is not an “asymmetric unescaping” scheme as described in the finding. While the overall approach could still be debated for other edge cases, the specific claim that unescaping is asymmetric and causes false "Illegal HTML" mismatches is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English bundle messages_en.properties is re-parsed for every translated file (N+1 shape), repeated disk I/O and parsing per verifier run

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, each call opens and parses both the target bundle (`new FileInputStream(file)` -> `new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)`) and an English bundle computed from the current file path (`String englishFile = ... _en.properties`; then `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` -> `new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)`). Since `verify()` is invoked per file, the same English `_en.properties` will be repeatedly read and re-parsed across many translated files, creating an N+1 style repeated disk I/O/parsing performance issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: File is read twice per verification: Files.readString loads contents for verifyNoDuplicateKeys then verifySafeHtml re-reads via new FileInputStream

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), the file is read once via Files.readString(file.toPath()) to run verifyNoDuplicateKeys(contents), and then verifySafeHtml() re-reads the same file using new FileInputStream(file) to build a PropertyResourceBundle. This is a real, diff-grounded inefficiency/redundant IO introduced by the change, but it does not by itself constitute broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(n²) string rebuilding in santizeAnchors due to repeated value.replaceFirst calls that recompile patterns and rebuild the whole string

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors`, the loop performs `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` on each matched anchor tag. Each `replaceFirst` creates a new regex pattern internally and rebuilds the whole `String`, so with multiple anchors this can lead to repeated full-string rebuilds (potentially O(n²) behavior). This is a performance/efficiency concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale matcher indices in santizeAnchors: modified value is not re-matched so matcher's indices refer to the pre-modification string, a latent correctness issue

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the `Matcher` is created from the original `value` and the loop uses only `matcher.find()` and `matcher.group()`; it does not use `matcher.start()/end()` or any indices that could become stale after `value` is modified. Although `value` is reassigned via `replaceFirst(...)`, the matcher’s positions are never consulted, so the specific claim about “stale matcher indices” causing a latent correctness issue is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-precompiled regexes in normalizeValue applied per key per locale file add avoidable Pattern.compile overhead

adjudication.rationale: In `normalizeValue(...)`, multiple calls to `String.replaceAll(...)` use regex literals (e.g., `"CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>"`, `"<Extensions>"`, `"\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}"`, and the email `style=...` removal). Each `replaceAll` compiles a new regex Pattern internally per invocation, and `normalizeValue` is called for every key/value processed in `verifySafeHtml()` across locale files. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern (not a correctness bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No caching/short-circuiting of sanitizer pipeline in verifySafeHtml; full pipeline runs even for keys with empty English values where a cheap HTML_TAGS pre-check would suffice

adjudication.rationale: The diff already reuses/caches the sanitizer configuration via the shared `PolicyFactory` fields (`POLICY_SOME_HTML` / `POLICY_NO_HTML`), so there isn’t an uncached “pipeline” being rebuilt per key. Also, even when `getEnglishValue()` returns an empty string (missing English key), `verifySafeHtml()` still must sanitize the translated `value` to enforce “no HTML” (`policy = POLICY_NO_HTML`), so a short-circuit based on empty English value would skip necessary validation, not just optimization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard RuntimeException thrown when English counterpart properties file is missing, escaping IOException handling and MojoExecutionException contract and crashing the verifier

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()`, only `IOException` from `Files.readString(...)` is wrapped into `MojoExecutionException`, but the newly added `verifySafeHtml()` throws `RuntimeException` on failures to read either the current properties file or its computed English counterpart (`new FileInputStream(englishFile)` in `verifySafeHtml()` catches `IOException` and rethrows `new RuntimeException(...)`). If the English `_en.properties` file is missing/unreadable, this will escape the method’s declared `MojoExecutionException` flow and can crash the verifier instead of returning a structured plugin error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English file path derived via brittle string mangling (replaceAll on locale suffix) that fails when no _en sibling exists or filename doesn't match the regex

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the English bundle path is derived via string replacement: `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`, and then unconditionally opened with `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If the derived `_en.properties` file does not exist (or the filename doesn’t match the locale-suffix regex so the replacement doesn’t produce the intended path), the code throws a `RuntimeException` (catching only `IOException`), aborting verification rather than reporting a normal validation message. This is a concrete, diff-introduced failure mode grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One bad file aborts verification of everything instead of accumulating messages

adjudication.rationale: The new HTML verification can throw unchecked exceptions that will stop the verifier instead of adding to `messages`. In `verify()`, only `IOException` from `Files.readString(...)` is caught, but `verifySafeHtml()` wraps failures reading the current file or the derived English file in `throw new RuntimeException(...)`. If e.g. `englishFile` doesn’t exist or can’t be read, verification will abort rather than accumulating a message for that file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml sanitizer allowlist (br, p, strong, b only) is narrower than real English message content, causing guaranteed false failures on legitimate translations

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, when the English source contains HTML it applies `POLICY_SOME_HTML` which only allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b` (no `<a>`). Many English messages in the diff clearly contain `<a ...>` (e.g., multiple `...BodyHtml` keys). The implementation compensates via `santizeAnchors()` by stripping anchor tags from the *translation* before sanitization, but it only does so when the anchor tag text matches the English anchor tag *exactly* (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`). This narrow allowlist + brittle exact-match stripping can produce false positives for otherwise “legitimate” translations that vary whitespace/attribute order/quoting while keeping the same anchor semantics. However, it’s not a guaranteed failure in all cases (anchors can match exactly), so this is better framed as a robustness/scope concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: containsHtml() only detects lowercase tags, so uppercase tags in English values wrongly force POLICY_NO_HTML on the translation

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.containsHtml(), HTML_TAGS is defined as `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source message contains uppercase/mixed-case HTML tags (e.g., `
`, `

`), `containsHtml(englishValue)` will return false and the verifier will apply `POLICY_NO_HTML` to the translation, potentially flagging otherwise-allowed HTML as illegal. This is a correctness defect in the newly added HTML detection logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors() mutates value while iterating a matcher over the original string, so replaceFirst deletes the wrong occurrence on repeated anchor tags

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors()`, although `value` is reassigned inside the `while (matcher.find())` loop, the loop’s logic does not depend on match indices/positions from the mutated string—only on the matched literal tag text (`matcher.group()` / `englishMatcher.group()`). The deletion uses `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` after confirming `matcher.group().equals(englishMatcher.group())`, so for repeated identical anchor tags it will remove one occurrence per iteration in sequence (the first remaining occurrence), not “the wrong occurrence” as claimed. The diff does not show a verifiable case where this would mis-delete due to the matcher being based on the original string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor mutation mismatch can emit spurious 'Didn't find anchor tag' error and break out of the loop, skipping remaining anchor checks
matched_golden_ids: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe a mismatch between anchor tags in the translated text vs the English source leading to incorrect validation behavior. The golden focuses on consuming English matcher groups without validating availability when the translation has extra anchors; the candidate highlights the resulting failure mode (spurious missing-anchor error and premature loop exit that skips further checks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor check is one-directional: missing anchors in translation compared to English are not detected, and requires byte-identical order and attributes

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, the code only iterates over anchor tags found in the translated `value` (`while (matcher.find())`) and never checks for any remaining anchors in the English source after the loop. Therefore, if the English string contains `<a...>` tags but the translation omits them entirely, this logic will not report it. Also, it compares `matcher.group()` and `englishMatcher.group()` with `Objects.equals(...)`, which requires the full matched tag text to be byte-identical (including attribute order/whitespace), and it advances `englishMatcher.find()` in lockstep, making the check order-dependent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_lt.properties totpStep1 uses Italian text in a Lithuanian message file
matched_golden_ids: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the Lithuanian locale file (messages_lt.properties) contains Italian text (specifically for totpStep1) and should be in Lithuanian instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_zh_CN.properties totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese characters in a Simplified Chinese bundle
matched_golden_ids: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag that the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) resource file contains Traditional Chinese wording/characters for the totpStep1 entry, implying an incorrect locale-appropriate translation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_fi/sk/sv totpStep1 strings drop app links and no longer match totpStep2/totpStep3 flow content

adjudication.rationale: In multiple community translations (e.g., themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_fi.properties, .../messages_sk.properties, .../messages_sv.properties) the `totpStep1` string was changed from naming/linking specific apps to a generic “Install one of the following applications…” text. The diff does not show any accompanying list being provided via message properties, so the phrase “following” may now be misleading/incomplete relative to `totpStep2`/`totpStep3` which proceed as if an authenticator app has been selected/installed. This is a content/i18n completeness issue rather than a verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No happy-path test asserting a clean properties file yields an empty messages list, so a regression flagging everything would still pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new validation logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and new tests only assert detection of failures (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) plus duplicate key detection. There is no test exercising a known-good properties file to assert `verify()` returns an empty `messages` list, so an overly strict/buggy sanitizer that flags all keys could still satisfy the current tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: santizeAnchors matching-anchor branch (value.replaceFirst mutation) has zero test coverage, and the replaceFirst logic itself is suspicious (removes first occurrence, not matched position, potentially mangling reordered/repeated anchors)

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, the “matching” branch (`if (englishMatcher.find() && Objects.equals(...)) { value = value.replaceFirst(...) }`) has no explicit test exercising the successful/allowed-anchor path. The added test `verifyNoChangedAnchors()` only covers the failure path (mismatched href -> adds "Didn't find anchor tag..."). Also, the matching logic is arguably fragile: it mutates `value` via `replaceFirst(...)` while iterating with a `Matcher` built from the original `value`, and it removes the first occurrence of the tag string rather than using the current match position—this could behave unexpectedly with reordered/repeated identical `<a...>` tags. These are diff-grounded concerns about robustness and test coverage, but not a clearly proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Break-after-message behavior for multiple mismatched anchors (only one message emitted) is never asserted

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), when an anchor tag in the translated value doesn’t match the next anchor tag in the English value, it adds one message ("Didn't find anchor tag ...") and then immediately `break`s out of the loop. The added test `verifyNoChangedAnchors()` only asserts that *a* "Didn't find anchor tag" message exists for a single-anchor fixture; it does not cover/lock in the behavior when there are multiple mismatched anchors (i.e., that only one message is emitted due to the `break`). This is a specific missing edge-case assertion for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing English file throws raw RuntimeException aborting the whole verification run instead of recording a message; English-path resolution uses fragile regex replaceAll

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, failure to open the computed English bundle (`new FileInputStream(englishFile)`) is caught as `IOException` and rethrown as a raw `RuntimeException` (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);`), which would abort the entire verification run rather than adding to `messages` like other checks. Additionally, `englishFile` is computed via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`; the unanchored `replaceAll` on the full absolute path is regex-fragile and can replace unintended substrings (e.g., matching underscores earlier in the path or multiple occurrences), increasing the chance of a missing/incorrect English path and triggering the abort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers a locale file with no _en counterpart or the resources-community to resources mapping

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` derives an English counterpart path via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` and then unconditionally opens it; missing files cause a `RuntimeException` (no graceful handling, unlike missing keys). The added tests (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties` with `noHtml_en.properties`, `changedAnchor_de.properties` with `changedAnchor_en.properties`) all have an `_en` counterpart and live under `misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources`, so they don’t exercise (a) a locale file without an `_en` file present or (b) the `resources-community`→`resources` path mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: normalizeValue special cases (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size choice-format, email RTL-style, entity-unescape) have no test coverage; the newly introduced {2,choice,...} exists to satisfy the normalization but no fixture pins that behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial key-specific normalization in `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue()` (special handling for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` choice patterns, plus HTML-entity unescape and email RTL-style stripping). The added tests (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`, duplicate keys) only exercise HTML sanitization/anchor checking and do not include fixtures/keys that trigger these normalization branches. Although the properties were updated to include `{2,choice,...}` (e.g., `error-invalid-multivalued-size=... {2,choice,...|1<values}`) and `templateHelp` was tweaked, no test fixture pins the intended normalization behavior for these cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties fixture causes an English-to-English self-comparison, so the English-source-contains-HTML allow branch and POLICY_SOME_HTML selection logic are never tested with a genuine translation pair

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the “English source” file path is derived by regex-replacing any locale suffix with “_en.properties”. When the fixture itself is already “illegalHtmlTag_en.properties”, that replacement yields the same path, so bundleEnglish is loaded from the same file as bundle (English-to-English comparison). This is diff-verifiable from: `String englishFile = file.getAbsolutePath()...replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties");` plus the test calling `getFile("illegalHtmlTag_en.properties")`. This doesn’t break product behavior, but it makes that particular test not exercise the intended translation-vs-English pairing behavior for the POLICY_SOME_HTML decision (it still hits the branch, but not with a distinct translation file).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile path-based English-file resolution via regex-munging absolute paths hard-codes maven module directory layout (resources-community → resources), breaking on directory renames or new layouts

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English reference bundle path is derived by munging the current file’s absolute path: `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This hard-codes assumptions about the repository/module directory layout (presence/naming of `resources-community` vs `resources`) and the filename locale pattern, making the verifier brittle to directory renames or alternative layouts. While it may work for the current structure, it’s a maintainability/robustness concern introduced by this diff rather than an immediately verifiable functional defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale-suffix regex [a-zA-Z-_]* doesn't match digit-containing locale tags (e.g. _es_419.properties), producing a nonexistent English file and an unhandled RuntimeException

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English file path is derived via `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This character class excludes digits, so filenames like `*_es_419.properties` would not match/replace the locale suffix, leaving `englishFile` pointing to a non-existent `.../messages_es_419.properties` in `resources` and causing `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` to throw, which is rethrown as an unchecked `RuntimeException` (not handled/converted to `MojoExecutionException`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: English-fallback resolution logic belongs in the caller (the Mojo), which knows which files are being verified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds English-fallback lookup inside `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` by deriving `englishFile` from the current `file` path via string replacements (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` and `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`) and then loading that file. This couples the verifier to a particular filesystem/layout convention instead of having the caller (the Mojo that selects/iterates files) provide the correct English baseline. That’s an architectural/scope concern introduced by the change, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: verifySafeHtml is a god-method (~100 lines) mixing file I/O, bundle loading, fallback resolution, normalization, sanitization, diffing and reporting, making per-key logic untestable in isolation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `verifySafeHtml()` in `VerifyMessageProperties.java` which is ~80+ lines and performs multiple responsibilities in one method: file I/O (opening `FileInputStream` twice), loading bundles and English fallback path computation, per-key normalization (`normalizeValue`), anchor handling (`santizeAnchors`), policy selection/sanitization, diff computation, and reporting via `messages.add(...)`. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue created by the change rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded per-key exception whitelist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) in Java code violates open/closed principle; every new message with special syntax requires a code change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `normalizeValue()` in `VerifyMessageProperties` with hard-coded per-key special cases (`key.equals("templateHelp")`, `key.equals("optimizeLookupHelp")`, and `key.startsWith("linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit") || key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size")`). This creates a maintenance/architecture concern: any future message key needing similar normalization (e.g., new placeholders containing `<...>` or `{...,choice,...}` patterns) would require modifying this Java code rather than being handled generically or via configuration. That’s an open/closed-principle style issue introduced by this change, but not a direct correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comparison pipeline correctness depends on reverse-engineering sanitizer implementation details (entity escaping, comment insertion), so bumping owasp-java-html-sanifier could cause mass false positives with no test asserting round-trip stability

adjudication.rationale: The new `verifySafeHtml()` logic explicitly compensates for specific OWASP sanitizer behaviors (comments in code: "Sanitizer will escape HTML entities..." and "Sanitizer will add them when there are double curly braces"; then `unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` and `sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`). This makes the comparison (`if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))`) sensitive to sanitizer output quirks, so a future `owasp-java-html-sanitizer` version change (added in pom at `20240325.1`) could alter escaping/comment behavior and produce widespread false positives. The added tests cover detection of illegal HTML / disallowed HTML / changed anchors, but none assert round-trip stability for these sanitizer-specific transformations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unnecessary explicit <scope>compile</scope> on commons-text adds noise

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a Maven dependency on `org.apache.commons:commons-text` with an explicit `<scope>compile</scope>` in `misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml`. While `compile` is Maven’s default scope (so the tag is arguably redundant), this is a minor style/configuration nit (“adds noise”), not a defect or a materially important review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded dependency versions (OWASP sanitizer, commons-text) in theme-verifier pom.xml duplicate centrally managed versions, creating duplication and CVE-tracking risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two new dependencies in misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml with explicit <version> values (owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1, commons-text 1.13.0). However, the finding’s core claim that these versions “duplicate centrally managed versions” and therefore create “duplication and CVE-tracking risk” cannot be verified from this diff alone because no parent POM or dependencyManagement section is shown to demonstrate an existing centrally managed version being bypassed/duplicated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public mutable instance fields POLICY_SOME_HTML / POLICY_NO_HTML should be private static final; POLICY_SOME_HTML being public leaks policy as API

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.java the fields are declared without an access modifier (`PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = ...;` and `PolicyFactory POLICY_NO_HTML = ...;`), so they are package-private, not `public`. The finding’s claim that they are “Public” and “leak policy as API” is not supported by the diff. While making them `private static final` could be a minor style/perf improvement, that is not what the finding asserts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pattern HTML_TAGS is an instance field without static despite ANCHOR_PATTERN below being private static final — inconsistent within the same class
matched_golden_ids: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point out that HTML_TAGS is being treated like a constant but is declared as an instance field, unlike other constants (e.g., ANCHOR_PATTERN) that are static final. The candidate doesn’t explicitly mention adding `final`/`private`, but the underlying issue (it should be a static constant per conventions/consistency) is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent error handling: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException, bypassing the established failure-signaling boundary

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, VerifyMessageProperties.verify() declares/uses MojoExecutionException as its error boundary (it catches IOException from Files.readString and rethrows MojoExecutionException). The newly added verifySafeHtml() instead catches IOException when reading PropertyResourceBundle and throws raw RuntimeException (e.g., `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + file, e);` and similarly for the English file). This bypasses the established MojoExecutionException failure signaling path, leading to inconsistent exception types and potentially less controlled reporting by the Maven plugin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: File read twice through two different mechanisms (Files.readString vs FileInputStream + PropertyResourceBundle), risking encoding divergence (ISO-8859-1 vs UTF-8) for non-Latin locale files

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), the file is read as text via Files.readString(file.toPath()) (UTF-8 by default) for verifyNoDuplicateKeys, but verifySafeHtml() rereads the same file using new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file)). PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) parses .properties using ISO-8859-1 rules, so for UTF-8-encoded locale files (which this repo appears to contain, given many non-ASCII literals in *.properties), the two reads can interpret characters differently, leading to incorrect HTML-safety comparisons and/or false errors in the verifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English source files are never actually validated: when the file being verified is the English file, the derived English path resolves to itself, so the value is compared against a sanitized copy of itself and always passes, leaving messages_en.properties unchecked for hostile HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `verifySafeHtml()` loads the current file into `bundle` and derives `englishFile` by regex replacement; for an `_en.properties` file this path can indeed resolve to the same file. However, it does not follow that the English file is “never validated” or “always passes”: the code still runs the OWASP sanitizer and compares `sanitized` vs `value`, which would flag illegal/non-allowed HTML (e.g., `<div>`, `<script>`) even in English. The only special-case is `santizeAnchors()`, which removes matching `<a...>` tags before sanitization; that can exempt anchor tags, but the finding’s blanket claim that `messages_en.properties` is unchecked because it compares against a sanitized copy of itself is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: English-file path regex is fragile: the character class includes '-' and '_' so basenames with hyphens or extra underscore segments (e.g. error-messages_de.properties) produce a wrong English filename, and the subsequent FileInputStream throws a bare RuntimeException that escapes verify()'s MojoExecutionException contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` which derives the English bundle path via `file.getAbsolutePath()...replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This regex can match from the first underscore through `.properties` (it’s greedy), so filenames with additional underscore segments before the locale (e.g., `error_messages_de.properties`) would be rewritten incorrectly (e.g., to `error_en.properties`). Also, `verifySafeHtml()` catches `IOException` and throws a raw `RuntimeException`, and `verify()` does not catch it, so it can escape the method’s `throws MojoExecutionException` contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages.properties (no locale suffix) doesn't match the regex at all and self-compares, so it is never validated

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English reference file is derived via `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. A properties file without a locale suffix (e.g., `messages.properties`) would not match this regex, so `englishFile` would remain the same base name (and potentially become the same file path), causing a self-compare rather than comparing against an `_en.properties` source. That weakens the intended rule ("only allow HTML in translations if English contains HTML") for such files, even though the file is still processed by the sanitizer (so the finding’s “never validated” phrasing is overstated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: MessageFormat syntax changes in JS apps' properties: switching from {{0}} to {0} / {2,choice,...} in account-ui and admin-ui messages_en.properties may render literally or fail since the JS frontends use their own interpolation, not Java MessageFormat, and the strings weren't verified against the JS interpolation code

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes placeholder syntax in JS app theme properties (e.g., `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`) from `{{0}} ... {{2}} value(s).` to Java/MessageFormat-style `{0} ... {2,choice,...}`. The diff does not show any corresponding change or verification in the JS account/admin UIs’ message interpolation logic, so there is a real compatibility risk that these strings could be rendered incorrectly if the JS i18n layer expected the previous `{{...}}` convention. However, the diff alone does not prove the JS frontends can’t handle MessageFormat, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor check is order-sensitive and one-shot: if a translation has fewer anchors than English (e.g. dropped email verification link), the loop ends silently and the translation passes verification

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), the loop iterates only over anchors found in the *translation* (ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)). If the translation contains fewer/zero <a> tags than the English source, the loop never executes (or finishes) and no error is added, so missing anchors are not detected. The check is also order-dependent because it advances a separate englishMatcher with englishMatcher.find() in lockstep with translation anchors, and it breaks on the first mismatch. Whether missing anchors should fail is not enforced by this logic (and not covered by tests), so this is a specific edge-case/coverage concern in the newly added verifier behavior rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor check breaks on the first mismatch, reporting only one error even if multiple anchors are malicious, and remaining anchor text causes a confusing generic 'Illegal HTML' diff instead of the real problem

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(...)`, the loop `while (matcher.find())` adds an error on the first mismatch and then `break`s, so additional malicious/incorrect `<a...>` tags later in the same value will not be specifically reported. After breaking, the remaining `<a>` tags will still be processed by the HTML sanitizer (which does not allow `a` even under `POLICY_SOME_HTML`), potentially producing an additional generic `Illegal HTML...` message; the verifier will still fail, but the diagnostics are incomplete/confusing rather than functionally incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anchor check requires anchors in identical order, so a valid translation that reorders link and text is falsely flagged

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.santizeAnchors(), anchor tags in the translated value are matched sequentially against anchor tags in the English value via two matchers advanced in lockstep (while (matcher.find()) { if (englishMatcher.find() && matcher.group().equals(englishMatcher.group())) ... else error }). This enforces identical order of / occurrences between source and translation; if a translation legitimately reorders multiple links, the verifier will report "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" even if the same anchor tags are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: containsHtml() pattern only matches lowercase tags, incorrectly denying HTML in translations when English has uppercase tags

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties, containsHtml() uses `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which matches only lowercase tag names. If an English source string contains HTML with uppercase/mixed-case tags (e.g., `
` or `
`), `containsHtml(englishValue)` will return false and the verifier will apply `POLICY_NO_HTML`, potentially flagging otherwise-acceptable translated HTML as illegal. This is a correctness defect in the newly added HTML-detection logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: containsHtml() false positives: English messages that merely mention angle-bracket text in prose flip the policy to POLICY_SOME_HTML for every translation of that key, permitting HTML where rendering escapes nothing

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `containsHtml()` only returns true if the English value matches `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, i.e., a lowercase HTML-like tag such as `
`, `

`, etc. Prose that merely mentions angle-bracket text like ``, ``, or numeric placeholders like `<1>` would not match this regex (uppercase/numeric), and `normalizeValue()` further strips known angle-bracket cases (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, and `{choice}` patterns with `<`). So the claim that “English messages that merely mention angle-bracket text in prose” will flip the policy to `POLICY_SOME_HTML` is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML allowlist mismatch: only br/p/strong/b are allowed though many Keycloak messages legitimately use <a>, <span>, <div>, producing both false passes and false failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff does define POLICY_SOME_HTML allowing only br/p/strong/b, but it also introduces explicit special handling for <a> via `santizeAnchors(...)`, which compares translation anchors to the English source and strips matching anchors before sanitization—so anchors are not simply “disallowed”. The claim that “many messages legitimately use <span>, <div>” is not verifiable from the diff (the only <div> appears in a new test fixture intended to be illegal).

adjudication_records.issue_text: normalizeValue unescapes HTML entities on both raw value and sanitized output, so the check validates the post-unescaping string while actual rendering depends on whether the frontend escapes entities, making the green light untrustworthy for entity-encoded payloads

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `normalizeValue()` unescaping HTML entities (`StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)`) and later also unescaping the sanitizer output before comparing. However, this does not make the check “green light untrustworthy” for entity-encoded payloads as claimed: by unescaping *before* sanitization, an entity-encoded tag like `<script>` becomes `<script>` and would be removed/altered by the OWASP sanitizer, causing the verifier to flag it (`sanitized != value`). The finding’s concern depends on unspecified frontend rendering/escaping behavior that is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_lt.properties:101 (account theme) replaces totpStep1 with Italian text in the Lithuanian file

adjudication.rationale: In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, the `totpStep1` value is changed from Lithuanian text to the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. This is a clear, diff-verifiable localization/correctness defect in the Lithuanian (lt) translation file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_zh_CN.properties:112 uses Traditional Chinese characters and drops FreeOTP/Play Store links

adjudication.rationale: In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties`, `totpStep1` is changed from a Simplified-Chinese string with links to a Traditional-Chinese phrasing (e.g., “您的手機”, “應用程式”) and the FreeOTP/Play Store/App Store anchor links are removed. This is directly visible in the diff and represents incorrect locale content for a `zh_CN` (Simplified) translation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: messages_fi/sk/sv drop all app-store/FreeOTP anchors and links entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows these translations removing the FreeOTP/App Store anchor tags/URLs entirely. For example, in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_fi.properties`, `totpStep1` changes from a sentence containing `FreeOTP` and `Google Play` to plain text with no links. Similar removals occur in `.../account/messages/messages_sk.properties` and `.../account/messages/messages_sv.properties`, and also in the login equivalents (`loginTotpStep1`) for `messages_sk.properties` and `messages_sv.properties`. This is a real, diff-grounded content/UX regression concern, but not a functional code defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Message diff substring logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when sanitized is a strict extension of value (start + end > value.length()), converting a clean verification failure into a plugin crash

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, when `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` it computes `start` as the common prefix length and `end` as the common suffix length, then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. There is no guard ensuring `value.length() - end >= start` (or same for `sanitized`). For certain sanitized transformations where the strings share the full value as prefix but also share some suffix characters (i.e., `start + end > value.length()`), `value.length() - end` becomes less than `start`, causing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` and crashing the plugin instead of reporting an illegal-HTML message.
